nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $S$ be a field that is an $R$-algebra, and let $M_1$, $M_2$ be vector spaces over $S$ that are also $R$-modules compatibly with $R \to S$. For a bilinear form $B$ over $S$ on such a space $M$ and an $R$-submodule $N$ of $M$, the dual of $N$ is $N^\vee = \{x \in M : B(x, y) \in R \text{ for all } y \in N\}$, where $R$ stands for its image in $S$. nodes.title: Dual submodule of an orthogonal product

nodes.summary: Let $B_1$ and $B_2$ be bilinear forms on modules $M_1$ and $M_2$ over a commutative semiring $R$. Their orthogonal product $B_1 \oplus B_2$ on $M_1 \times M_2$ is nondegenerate (both left- and right-separating) if and only if $B_1$ and $B_2$ are both nondegenerate.
nodes.title: Nondegeneracy of an orthogonal product

nodes.summary: Let $B_1$ and $B_2$ be bilinear forms on modules $M_1$ and $M_2$ over a commutative semiring $R$, with orthogonal product $B_1 \oplus B_2$ on $M_1 \times M_2$. For all $x = (x_1, x_2)$ and $y = (y_1, y_2)$ in $M_1 \times M_2$, $(B_1 \oplus B_2)(x, y) = B_1(x_1, y_1) + B_2(x_2, y_2)$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of an orthogonal product

nodes.summary: Let $B_1$ and $B_2$ be bilinear forms on modules $M_1$ and $M_2$ over a commutative semiring $R$. Their orthogonal product $B_1 \oplus B_2$ is the bilinear form on $M_1 \times M_2$ given by $(B_1 \oplus B_2)((x_1, x_2), (y_1, y_2)) = B_1(x_1, y_1) + B_2(x_2, y_2)$.
nodes.title: Orthogonal product of bilinear forms
